audit_findings.title: The trend anchor spans economically incomparable acquisition perimeters
audit_findings.mechanism: The non-comparable OE history directly determines the $285.7 million anchor and may also distort inferred growth; every scenario operating PV depends on that anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Accordingly, prior periods within these consolidated financial statements may not be comparable.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated: NuVasive entered in September 2023, Nevro entered in April 2025, and the filing expressly says prior periods may not be comparable. The valuation nevertheless fits one absolute-dollar trend across those periods. The direction is unresolved because a constant-perimeter reconstruction could raise earlier OE, lower acquisition-driven apparent growth, or both. Because this affects the central earnings base supporting $3.399-$4.483 billion of operating value, it is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild annual OE on a pro-forma constant perimeter, or separately bridge legacy Globus, NuVasive and Nevro OE, then recompute the log trend, anchor and all scenarios without changing the stated valuation rules.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration may disappear from both the bridge and share count
audit_findings.magnitude: $105.389 million at 2026-06-30; $0.72 per share if entirely deducted as cash, equal to 2.1%-2.6% of supplied scenario equity values; maximum RSU dilution unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The cash-settled portion belongs in the equity bridge, while the RSU-settled portion belongs in fully diluted shares; the same obligation must not be counted in both places.
audit_findings.evidence: The contingent payments for this acquisition are based upon achieving various performance milestones over a period of 10 years and are payable in a combination of cash and RSUs.
audit_findings.explanation: A recorded acquisition liability is demonstrated and the latest filed amount is $105.389 million, not the year-end $101.508 million. Its cash-versus-RSU allocation remains unresolved. On an intentionally conservative all-cash comparison, deducting the entire carrying value reduces value by only $0.72 per share, versus supplied values of $27.46-$34.91 and a market price of $78.29, so the recorded expected obligation cannot change the valuation conclusion. The contractual maximum RSU exposure should still be checked because it is not disclosed in the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $105.389 million June 2026 balance by acquisition and settlement form, deduct only the expected cash portion, add unsettled probability-weighted RSUs to diluted shares, and verify the contractual maximum without double counting.

audit_findings.title: The gross-cash bridge may omit the accrued Pimenta settlement claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $43.1 million; $0.30 per share and 0.8%-1.1% of supplied scenario equity values
audit_findings.mechanism: If the accrued award remains unpaid and its cash settlement is not represented in forecast OE, it reduces cash available in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we have recorded a liability of $ 43.1 million, which includes our accrual for interest and costs based on the Court's order, in our accrued expenses.
audit_findings.explanation: The $43.1 million judgment, interest and cost accrual is demonstrated, and the June 2026 filing reports no additional charge while legal and settlement accruals remain on the balance sheet. Whether the fitted anchor already captures an economically equivalent burden requires placement analysis, but even a full separate bridge deduction would reduce value by only $0.30 per share. That is too small relative to the $27.46-$34.91 valuation range and $78.29 market price to change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the Pimenta-specific balance and payment status at June 30, 2026; if unpaid and not represented in forecast OE, deduct $43.1 million from excess cash and rerun the bridge, while preventing double counting of the retained 2025 litigation charge.

audit_findings.title: Finite and noncash tax benefits may contaminate the exceptional 2025 OE observation
audit_findings.magnitude: $46.3 million valuation-allowance release and $117.7 million non-taxable bargain-purchase gain; the release alone equals 16.2% of the $285.7 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unpurged tax benefit inflates 2025 OE, affects the fitted anchor, and may cause the forecast and terminal period to use an unsustainably low cash-tax burden.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2025, the decrease in the effective tax rate was primarily due to the release of valuation allowances on certain deferred tax assets of $46.3 million and the impact of the non-taxable bargain purchase gain of $117.7 million in the second quarter of the year ended December 31, 2025, with no comparable event in the prior period.
audit_findings.explanation: The exceptional tax items are demonstrated, but contamination of OE is not yet demonstrated because the supplied record does not show the OE calculation trace. The risk is material: the $46.3 million valuation-allowance release alone is 16.2% of the anchor, and the filed effective tax rate rose from 11.1% in 2025 to 20.5% for the first half of 2026 after the one-time benefits. If the release or finite NOL benefits were capitalized as recurring OE, the anchor and terminal earning power would be overstated.
audit_findings.action: Trace 2025 OE from reported earnings through removal of the $117.7 million bargain-purchase gain, deferred-tax items and actual cash taxes; then normalize prospective cash taxes after finite NOLs and credits and rerun the trend, anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved patent litigation remains outside both OE and the equity bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: Damages or settlement would reduce the equity bridge; royalties, redesign costs or lost Modulus sales from an injunction would reduce future OE and possibly growth.
audit_findings.evidence: The litigation is currently ongoing, and the outcome of this litigation cannot be determined, nor can we estimate a range of potential loss; therefore, we have not recorded a liability, outside of counsel fees, related to this litigation as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The ongoing 4WEB litigation and absence of a recorded liability are demonstrated, but an adverse outcome is only a possibility. The company states that neither the outcome nor a loss range can be estimated, and the record supplies no Modulus revenue, margin, royalty exposure, insurance or indemnification data. The matter may affect value, but the supplied evidence cannot establish its magnitude or materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the latest procedural status, Modulus revenue and contribution margin, asserted damages or royalty theories, injunction exposure, and insurance or indemnification coverage; then probability-weight any supportable operating or bridge adjustment and rerun the affected scenarios.
